sources.title: Russia suffers record troop losses in October, its worst month since full-scale invasion, Ukraine says
sources.text: War Russia suffers record troop losses in October, its worst month since full-scale invasion, Ukraine says November 1, 2026 11:30 am • 3 min read Prefer on Google by Chris Powers Photo for illustrative purposes: A fallen Russian soldier's belongings in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2024.(Jose Colon/Anadolu via Getty Images) Russia's combat losses were greater in October 2026 than in any other month since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the General Staff of Ukraine's Armed Forces reported. According to the data from the General Staff, Russia's estimated losses reached 54,400 soldiers in October. That's 8,170 more than in the previous month. The figure includes those killed, wounded, and missing in action. "This is a record for any month of the full-scale war," said President Volodymyr Zelensky on social media. Zelensky also mentioned that in October, Ukraine liberated more territory than it lost, 96.2 square kilometers (37.1 square miles) vs 85.8 square kilometers (33.1 square miles) occupied by Russia. In October, our Ukrainian Defence Forces inflicted record losses on the enemy and recaptured more territory than the Russian occupiers were able to seize. "We thank all our defenders, all our soldiers, every brigade and every unit for this result, which is so important for our country. Russia is losing," Zelensky said. The General Staff said the high rate matters because it "exceeds the enemy's ability to replenish its units. Every month of the war is costing the Russian army more and more." The National Guard's 1st Azov Corps said a significant share of Moscow's losses stemmed from Russia's offensive in the direction of the city of Dobropillia , in Donetsk Oblast. A Month of Record Losses for Russian Occupiers In October, Russian forces suffered their highest personnel losses since 2022. A significant portion of these losses occurred within the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps of the National Guard of Ukraine “Azov”, one of the key… pic.twitter.com/6bvn4NqUEU — First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine (@azov_media) October 31, 2026 The Corps estimates it has killed, wounded, and captured over 6,800 Russian troops in "one of the key axes of the Russian offensive." October was also a record month for Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, its commander Robert "Magyar" Brovdi wrote on social media. Brovdi said that his forces hit a Russian soldier every 159 seconds in October, averaging 542 casualties daily. The more Russia racks up combat losses, the greater the need for Moscow to increase its own mobilization efforts. President Volodymyr Zelensky warned in August that Russia plans to mobilize around 300,000 people after its September election is out of the way. So far, Moscow announced plans to conscript an additional 120,000 people on Oct. 2. "Ukrainian Defense Forces will continue to inflict losses on the occupiers until the complete cessation of Russia's armed aggression against Ukraine," said the General Staff. According to the General Staff, Russia has lost 1,590,270 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy. Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1." A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to have been killed in action. read also ‘I don’t know if negotiated peace is achievable,’ Rubio says as uncertainty hangs over Russia-Ukraine talks Russia Ukraine Ukrainian armed forces Azov Russian armed forces Russian losses
